open_points.subject: A1: Accepted decision A1 — What a file of the folder becomes
open_points.text:
Files are visited folder by folder: the files of a folder in order of their names, then its
subfolders in order of their names, compared by Unicode code point.
open_points.question: How is a filesystem name that is not valid Unicode represented, ordered and returned in M02: is the scan refused, is the entry skipped, or is a reversible byte-to-string representation used?
options: Refuse the whole scan with FOLDER_UNAVAILABLE
Skip the unrepresentable entry
Represent arbitrary filename bytes reversibly and order those represented values
open_points.default_guess: Use the platform's reversible surrogate representation, order the resulting code points, and preserve it through the name field.

witness.initial: The photo folder contains a regular file whose name includes the byte 0xFF and whose content is otherwise a valid supported image.
events: The owner asks the calling flow to scan the project.
The deliverer lists and orders the folder entries.
outcomes: The scan reports the file under a reversible string name.
The scan skips the file or refuses the operation because its name is not valid Unicode.
witness.observer: The owner through the calling flow

open_points.subject: A1: Accepted decision A1 — What a file of the folder becomes
open_points.text: INV-01: after a scan, a placement, a repeated placement and a mark, the source folder holds the same files with the same bytes, modification times and modes (`test_no_operation_changes_the_source_folder`).
open_points.question: Must INV-01 also preserve access times, ownership, ACLs and extended attributes, or is the required assertion deliberately limited to files, bytes, modification times and modes?
options: Preserve every filesystem datum, including access time
Assert only the properties explicitly listed in the Required tests item
Permit incidental access-time changes but preserve all other metadata
open_points.default_guess: Treat incidental access-time changes caused by reads as allowed and assert exactly the listed properties.

witness.initial: The filesystem updates a file's access time when its contents are read.
events: The owner requests a scan that reads the file.
The filesystem advances the file's access time without changing its bytes, modification time or mode.
outcomes: INV-01 passes because the Required tests item does not include access time.
INV-01 fails because changing access time changes something in the source folder.

open_points.subject: A1: Accepted decision A1 — What a file of the folder becomes
open_points.text: INV-02: a delivery opens no path that fails condition 1 of A3 rule 5.
open_points.question: Does INV-02 prohibit opening any component of a name that ultimately fails condition 1, or does it permit opening the validated prefix needed to discover the failing component, as A3 rule 5 requires?
options: Open no component of an ultimately failing path
Open each validated prefix component but not the failing component's target or anything beyond it
open_points.default_guess: Open the validated prefix components needed for the check, but never open the named file, a component past the failure, or a symbolic-link target.

witness.initial: The requested name is `safe/missing/photo.jpg`; `safe` is a real folder and `missing` is absent.
events: A3 rule 5 requires the deliverer to open the photo folder and each folder of the name in turn to decide condition 1.
outcomes: The deliverer opens `safe`, discovers that `missing` is absent and refuses.
The deliverer opens none of the path because the complete name fails condition 1.
witness.observer: A file-open trace used by the INV-02 test

open_points.subject: A1: Accepted decision A1 — What a file of the folder becomes
open_points.text: INV-02: for content with no placement, an empty or absolute name, a name with an empty, `.` or `..` segment, an ignored name at any level, a folder, and a path through a symbolic link each fail with the NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT member of = models.PlacementFailure and add no file except the project lock, and a trace of every file the process opens while the delivery runs shows no opening of the named file, of a folder past the segment that fails or of a link's target (`test_a_name_a_scan_would_not_report_is_not_delivered`).
open_points.question: What must the INV-02 witness show for the other condition-1 cases—an absent folder or final segment, a non-folder component, a folder-opening failure, and an unreadable final metadata record?
options: Add explicit cases and open-trace assertions for every condition-1 branch
Treat the listed examples as sufficient representatives of all condition-1 branches
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit cases for every materially distinct condition-1 branch.

open_points.subject: A2: Accepted decision A2 — What reaches the Portal store
open_points.text:
A camera value is unusable when it is malformed, when its UTC year
   is before the imported `CAMERA_EARLIEST_YEAR` constant, or when it is more than the imported
   `CAMERA_LATEST_AFTER_MODIFIED_HOURS` constant of hours after the file's modification time.
open_points.question: What exact EXIF date-time syntax is well formed, and are fractional seconds from fields such as `SubSecTimeOriginal` read, ignored, or grounds for falling back to the next time source?
options: Accept only the base EXIF date-time field to whole seconds and ignore subsecond companion fields
Combine the base field with a valid EXIF subsecond companion field
Accept an explicitly defined broader parser grammar
open_points.default_guess: Parse the standard base EXIF form to whole seconds and ignore subsecond companion fields unless they are explicitly added to the design.

witness.initial: A file has `DateTimeOriginal` equal to `2026:11:20 10:15:30` and `SubSecTimeOriginal` equal to `750`; its modification time is later.
events: The deliverer derives `taken_at` and the publication `photo_date`.
outcomes: The subsecond field is ignored and the delivered instant is `2026-11-20T10:15:30`.
witness.observer: The owner and Portal through the publication body

open_points.subject: A2: Accepted decision A2 — What reaches the Portal store
open_points.text:
Only the first frame of an animated
   image is delivered.
open_points.question: Must the photo moment also be read exclusively from the first frame's metadata, or may it come from container-level or another frame's EXIF metadata?
options: Use only EXIF associated with the first frame
Use the image library's container-level EXIF result
Search frames for the first usable EXIF value
open_points.default_guess: Use only the metadata exposed for the first frame, matching the pixels that are delivered.

witness.initial: An animated source has no date on its first frame and a usable `DateTimeOriginal` on its second frame.
events: The deliverer selects the first frame's pixels and derives the photo moment.
outcomes: It falls back to the file modification time because the first frame has no usable camera time.
It uses the second frame's camera time although the second frame's pixels are not delivered.
witness.observer: The owner through the resulting photo date

open_points.subject: A2: Accepted decision A2 — What reaches the Portal store
open_points.text:
For a source
   it opens, checks run in this order: a first frame whose width times height is above the imported
   `MAX_PIXELS` constant fails with the TOO_MANY_PIXELS member, a source that cannot be decoded with the
   UNREADABLE_IMAGE member, and a result longer than the imported `MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES` constant, the Portal's
   read limit, with the TOO_LARGE member.
open_points.question: What outcome applies when decoding succeeds but orientation, conversion, resizing, compositing or JPEG encoding fails before a result exists?
options: Return the UNREADABLE_IMAGE placement failure
Return the UNREADABLE_FILE placement failure
Refuse the whole operation with a service-state refusal
Treat the failure as an unhandled internal error
open_points.default_guess: Return the UNREADABLE_IMAGE placement failure for any deterministic image-processing or encoding failure before storage.

open_points.subject: A3: Accepted decision A3 — One placement per project and content
open_points.text:
Delivering content that already has a placement answers `replayed` with the stored placement and the
   current `photo_id` of its mark, if any, and writes nothing, whatever name the request carries and even
   when the source file has left the folder.
open_points.question: Because the project lock is taken before the existing-placement check, does creating or updating a durable lock artifact violate the replay rule's “writes nothing,” or is the project lock an allowed exception?
options: A replay may create or update the project lock
The lock must already exist or be implemented without durable writes
“Writes nothing” excludes lock infrastructure but only when another rule says so
open_points.default_guess: Require lock acquisition to make no durable change observable as application state during a replay.

witness.initial: A placement already exists, but no project-lock file exists on disk.
events: The caller repeats delivery of that content.
The service reaches the project-lock check before looking up the placement.
outcomes: The service creates a lock file and returns `replayed`.
The service uses a non-durable lock or refuses to create a lock artifact so that replay writes nothing.
witness.observer: The operator inspecting durable files and the INV-06 test

open_points.subject: A3: Accepted decision A3 — One placement per project and content
open_points.text: INV-06: a second placement returns the first publication and leaves every stored image and placement record unchanged, with one placement record in place (`test_a_repeated_placement_writes_no_durable_state`). When no refusal of A6 rule 5 applies, a delivery repeated after a failed record write completes the placement (`test_a_delivery_repeated_after_a_failed_record_write_completes`).
open_points.question: Must the Required tests item demonstrate the “at most one placement” invariant under concurrent first deliveries, or is a sequential second delivery sufficient?
options: Require a concurrent-delivery witness that ends with one placement
Treat sequential replay plus the separately specified locking tests as sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Add a concurrent first-delivery witness that asserts one placement record and one effective stored image.

open_points.subject: A3: Accepted decision A3 — One placement per project and content
open_points.text: INV-07: a replaced file is reported as a new `ready` photo while the earlier image and mark stay (`test_a_replaced_file_is_a_new_photo_and_the_first_delivery_stays`), and a removed file keeps its delivery (`test_removing_a_file_keeps_its_delivery`).
open_points.question: For removal, must the test explicitly assert that the earlier placement record, stored image and publication mark are all byte-for-byte unchanged, as INV-07 states?
options: Explicitly assert all three durable artifacts remain unchanged
Treat “keeps its delivery” as sufficient to imply all three
open_points.default_guess: Explicitly assert the placement record, stored image and publication mark remain unchanged.

open_points.subject: A7: Accepted decision A7 — Time
open_points.text:
The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding
open_points.question: When the system clock supplies a value finer than a microsecond, which microsecond is produced—must the excess fraction be truncated toward the earlier instant, as file modification time is, or is another conversion allowed?
options: Drop the excess fraction toward the earlier instant
Use the host datetime conversion's behavior
Require the backend clock itself to supply an already microsecond-exact value
open_points.default_guess: Drop any finer fraction toward the earlier instant.

events: The calling flow records a publication mark.
The mark reads `utc_now` once and stores `marked_at`.
outcomes: The backend conversion produces another microsecond value, such as `2026-11-20T10:15:30.123457`, or rejects the reading.
witness.observer: The caller reading the mark and the persisted M07 record

open_points.subject: A7: Accepted decision A7 — Time
open_points.text: INV-13: a counting clock is read once by a mark and not at all by a scan, a delivery or the health answer (`test_only_the_mark_reads_the_clock`), and `marked_at` equals that reading (`test_a_marked_photo_is_reported_as_published`).
open_points.question: What must the INV-13 test show for a mark refused before the clock point, a mark refused after it, and a replayed mark?
options: Test zero reads before the point and exactly one read for post-point refusal and replay
Test only one successful new mark because it represents all mark paths
open_points.default_guess: Add separate assertions for pre-clock refusal, post-clock refusal and replay, matching normative rule 2.

open_points.subject: A1: Accepted decision A1 — What a file of the folder becomes
open_points.text:
| Order | Condition | Status | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | empty | `rejected` | `empty` |
| 2 | larger than the source limit | `rejected` | `too_large` |
| 3 | opened in non-blocking mode without following a link, what it finds is not a regular file | `rejected` | `not_a_regular_file` |
| 4 | it grew past the source limit while being read | `rejected` | `too_large` |
| 5 | opening or reading it fails, which includes a file that disappeared or became a symbolic link after its metadata was read | `rejected` | `unreadable_file` |
| 6 | does not begin with the signature of a format of the imported `SOURCE_FORMATS` constant: for no format do all the rows of the imported `SOURCE_SIGNATURES` constant with that `format` find their `signature` bytes at their `offset` | `rejected` | `unsupported_format` |
| 7 | placed and marked | `published` | none |
| 8 | placed | `placed` | none |
| 9 | anything else | `ready` | none |
open_points.rule:
**Член перечисления** note называет его именем рядом с адресом перечисления:
`the EXPENSE_CREATE member of = models.AuditAction`.
open_points.question: Replace every status and reason value with its generated member name beside the address of = models.ScanStatus or = models.ObservationReason.

open_points.subject: A1: Accepted decision A1 — What a file of the folder becomes
open_points.text:
A signature does not prove that an image can be decoded: a `ready`
file may still fail when it is delivered.
open_points.rule:
**Член перечисления** note называет его именем рядом с адресом перечисления:
`the EXPENSE_CREATE member of = models.AuditAction`.
open_points.question: Name the READY member of = models.ScanStatus instead of naming it only by its value.

open_points.subject: A3: Accepted decision A3 — One placement per project and content
open_points.text:
Delivering content that already has a placement answers `replayed` with the stored placement and the
   current `photo_id` of its mark, if any, and writes nothing, whatever name the request carries and even
   when the source file has left the folder.
open_points.rule:
**Член перечисления** note называет его именем рядом с адресом перечисления:
`the EXPENSE_CREATE member of = models.AuditAction`.
open_points.question: Name the REPLAYED member of = models.PlacementStatus beside the enumeration address.

open_points.subject: A3: Accepted decision A3 — One placement per project and content
open_points.text: INV-07: a replaced file is reported as a new `ready` photo while the earlier image and mark stay (`test_a_replaced_file_is_a_new_photo_and_the_first_delivery_stays`), and a removed file keeps its delivery (`test_removing_a_file_keeps_its_delivery`).
open_points.rule:
**Член перечисления** note называет его именем рядом с адресом перечисления:
`the EXPENSE_CREATE member of = models.AuditAction`.
open_points.question: Name the READY member of = models.ScanStatus beside the enumeration address.
